hypotheses.title: Long-Horizon Option Breakeven Asymmetry and Upside Expansion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In the options market (option9), institutional investors express directional skew and tail-risk expectations through out-of-the-money positioning. The 180-day call breakeven (call_breakeven_180) reflects open-interest weighted institutional upside price targets, while put_breakeven_180 reflects structural downside hedging floors. When a stock's rolling 60-day standardized upside distance expands relative to its downside distance within its subindustry, it signals aggressive institutional upside call accumulation and expanding forward return expectations.
confounders: Unhedged earnings release volatility where deep OTM lottery calls artificially elevate call breakeven
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if rolling 60-day breakeven asymmetry generates Sharpe < 1.25 or fails sub-universe consistency in TOP3000.

candidates.expression: group_zscore(ts_zscore((call_breakeven_180 - close) / close, 60) - ts_zscore((close - put_breakeven_180) / close, 60), subindustry)
candidates.rationale: Subindustry-standardized spread of 60-day rolling z-scores of upside call breakeven distance versus downside put breakeven distance.

hypotheses.title: Idiosyncratic Variance Compression with Low-Beta and Market Coupling Synergy
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical asset pricing confirms the low-beta and low-volatility anomaly: equities with high idiosyncratic uncertainty deliver inferior risk-adjusted performance due to lottery preferences and flighty retail capital. In the systematic risk model (model51), penalizing short-term idiosyncratic risk (-unsystematic_risk_last_30_days) and market sensitivity (-beta_last_60_days_spy) while rewarding persistent market correlation (correlation_last_30_days_spy) isolates structurally stable, high-conviction institutional compounding equities with low drawdown profiles.
confounders: Sudden macro factor rotation regimes where high-beta speculative equities rally aggressively during market recoveries
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if low-beta and idiosyncratic compression synergy fails to achieve Sharpe >= 1.25 or Fitness >= 1.00.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-standardized synthesis of low idiosyncratic risk, low market beta, and market correlation coupling.

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Customer Return Spillover Lead-Lag Arbitrage
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In corporate supply chain networks (pv13), customer cash flow and stock price shocks propagate downstream to supplier equities with a latency of several trading days due to delayed retail and institutional order-flow assimilation. Linearly decaying customer return signals (ts_decay_linear(pv13_custretsig_retsig, 10)) capture incoming supplier revenue momentum. Subtracting the supplier's own short-term price return (ts_delta(close, 5) / close) creates an unpriced lead-lag catch-up arbitrage signal.
confounders: Supplier customer loss announcements or product obsolescence that breaks historical supply chain revenue transmission
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if customer return spillover fails to achieve Sharpe >= 1.25 or if turnover exceeds 70% in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized spread between 10-day decayed customer return momentum and supplier 5-day price reaction.
